scores.strengths: States-not-messages is the right substrate for someone who hates nagging: a light's level is a re-evaluated predicate that says nothing, so it cannot nag, and the single slot is the only voice. Every nudge cites a number already on screen (verify nudge -> rework cell, cache nudge -> cache cell). Faithful to every verified correction I checked: C001 5m-TTL tightening and no countdown above 300 s, C002 dedupe by message.id + write-rate pricing + 'idle' not 'expected', C003 two tiers with plan-exit struck and /clear 'cheap', C005 p50 19 not 32 + subscriber wording, C017 synthetic filter, C018 post-only, C023 batching_reminder dropped, C026 live-gap primary, C030 doc-only suppression + degrade-to-strip when no test cmd, C032 git-tick numstat, C043 no commit-only trigger + '?' allowed, C050 never bare Bash, C055 test vs build/lint split, C057/C058 loop signature, C059 demoted to strip token, C060 spend-limit branch, C062 NOW exempt from first-2-turn/away, C064 verb truncates. 'v' is genuinely free (src/app.rs key arms: ?,1-9,Tab,Esc,p,w,+/-,q,a,t,L,S,space) and `pub view: View` matches both VIEW-01's recommended pattern and PRD US-009. Mockup verified at 56 cells; degrades to 22-char light rows at 40 cols. 'next' + 'snoozed' rows make silence visibly deliberate; toasts only on NOW promotion; cache-miss is LATER with no toast (C002 says informational). Events audit trail (fired/acted/snoozed) is the only design that plans to tune rules against real behaviour.
scores.weaknesses: Context light goes ● at >=300k on a 1M window, which for this owner (sessions at 400-950k) means a red light most of the day that cannot be snoozed - wallpaper risk the design does not address. No explore-run delegation nudge (A05's Bash-aware successor) and no plan-first line, so one rework lever is left on the dashboard. Ranking by tokens x remaining calls favours context/cache over rework within a class (acknowledged, unmeasured). OSC 52 clipboard is not implemented today (ask.rs uses pbcopy/wl-copy/xclip) - fine as a fallback chain but the claim is aspirational. Ambiguous-width glyphs (○ ◐ ● ▸ ↻ ✓) need the ASCII theme fallback before the pane at ambiguous=wide terminals. Single slot hides a second simultaneous problem behind n/N.
scores.steal: Self-fixes rather than grafts: (1) make ● on the context light depend on 'clean stop available' or limit share, not ctx alone, so a deliberate 1M session is amber, not permanently red; (2) add Radar's 'soon' phrasing that names the firing condition ('no-check nudge at 10m/14c') to the 'next' row; (3) add Phase Coach's >=4-in-5 corpus wrong-rate bar as the admission test for the slot; (4) add Ticker's `next 19c ≈$4.4 vs fresh $0.9` comparison as the context light's 1-key detail and the t toggle to rate-limit units for subscribers; (5) add an explore-run LATER nudge (Esc + re-prompt wording, not 'queue', since queued prompts land at turn end 26/28).

scores.strengths: Most complete lever coverage of the four (explore-delegate, plan-first, check, corrections, cascade, denied, steers, silent-run, destructive git, screenshots, agents, commit-green, review, checkpoint, ctx-cost, drift, post-compact, waiting, cache countdown, cold resume, switch, loop, API error, cache miss, prefix, loop health). Two ideas nobody else has: a corpus wrong-rate bar (>=4 in 5 right to take the ▸ slot; N-PLAN-FEATURE rendered dim because it cannot meet it) and an acted/retired history in the idle view ('acted · cargo test ran 31 s later') that shows the coach stops when you act. VERIFY rendered only as the literal command + age (per C041/C055 corrections). Data prerequisites enumerated honestly and completely; Mode::Coach via layout::solve's existing force param per the C064 correction; mockup rows verified at 56 cells with tiles <=26 chars per the C041 layout correction. Engine-native overrides in the pane (tool.check rule, classic PreModelSwitch, Spinner.mode) are correctly scoped.
scores.weaknesses: Density: 20 rows carrying four advice-bearing regions (passive per-phase 'next:' line, NOW slot, NEXT line, soon line) - more than C062's 'one nudge + one soon', and the 'next:' line is a static per-phase sentence that will become wallpaper ('let it run - a check lands <=2 calls after edits'). N-EXPLORE-DELEGATE's action ('type the line, Enter without Esc - lands at Claude's next API call') contradicts the C030 verdict (26/28 queued prompts land at turn end) and the design's own N-CHECK wording, so the mid-run delegation nudge would rarely take effect in time. Twelve phase words rest on a 94% self-consistency figure and a 47-56% verify agreement, and the phase gate makes nudge eligibility depend on that classifier. Toasts include live cache-miss (informational per C002) - an after-the-fact cost toast is a nag. The pane's [1 stop turn] $.turn.abort button is a write to the session, against the pane PRD §6 read-only stance. 'sess $' sourced from cost-state, which is written only at shutdown/resume (C014 verdict) - must be the ledger sum instead.
scores.steal: The >=4-in-5 corpus wrong-rate admission bar for the slot; acted-vs-retired history with the observable completion shown in idle; the phase gate as a filter on nudge eligibility (not as a displayed word); N-PLAN-FEATURE as a dim, never-toasting line; loop-health indicator replacing the slot in session_mode=loop; the explicit snapshot fixture list (8-call explore run, Edit->cargo test->commit, unverified commit, AskUserQuestion with >1 h gap, /clear, TaskUpdate completed, <synthetic> line); pane overrides from engine-native fields (tool.check rule for the exact allow-rule, classic.PreModelSwitch, Spinner.mode).

scores.strengths: The `next 19c ≈$4.4 · fresh $0.9` tile is the single best decision number in any design - it makes continue-vs-/compact-vs-/clear decidable at a glance and uses the session's own p50 run length per the C005 correction. Tape of priced events (>=20k tokens or >=$0.10) is a genuine audit surface for 'where did the money go' without telling the person what to do. Agents tile with failed-spawn count reflects the C014 correction (174/264 <synthetic> spawns excluded). `t` toggle to rate-limit units defaulting on when rate_limits is present honours C005/C024. `soon` armed during the turn; last-3-retired shown in the why overlay; Enter reuses the existing ask popup (copy / S-send over the session socket, docs/socket.md) so nothing new is invented. Corrections applied faithfully (C001, C002, C003, C005, C007, C010, C014, C016, C017, C018, C026, C030, C032, C035, C037, C040, C042, C043, C044, C050, C054, C060). Mockup verified at 56 cells.
scores.weaknesses: Cost-first ranking demotes rework: in the busy mockup a running agent at 398k beats 'no ✓ 8m' (amber in the state line) because priced saving wins within the NOW class, and the six tiles carry no edits/fails/denied counters - for a Max subscriber whose $ are notional (C005 verdict) the frame optimises a number the person does not pay. cache-miss-priced is NOW -> toast on every >=20k miss including previous_message_not_found idle returns (~80/month) - C002 says informational, so this is an after-the-fact nag; cold-resume also toasts at attach. `t` collides with the global theme key and `?` with global help while the text also says '? help as today' - contradictory; mockup shows agents ≈$117 (stale snapshot) where the corrected figure is $897. The ×3.2 7d multiplier needs per-turn medians baseline.rs lacks (BASE-01) and is hidden below 3 sessions - honest, but the headline tile is then blank early. No silent-run liveness indicator, no stacked-steers token, no uncommitted line in the tiles, no explore-delegate or plan-first. ctx-price re-fires every +100k on a deliberate long task (acknowledged 'marginal as a nudge').
scores.steal: `next 19c ≈$4.4 · fresh $0.9` continue-vs-reset comparison (as the context light's detail / why overlay headline); `t` toggle between $ and rate-limit weight (fable 10 / opus 5 / sonnet 3 / haiku 1) defaulting to limit units when rate_limits is present; agents figure with 'N failed (spend limit)'; the priced-events tape as an Events-panel kind=cost filter on the dashboard, not in the coach view; `soon` line armed mid-turn for the turn-end checkpoint; last-3-retired with reason in the why overlay; per-turn 7d median once baseline.rs gains it; Enter on an event row opening the same why overlay.

scores.strengths: Cleanest cause-and-effect contract: each counter names the keystroke that resets it and the nudge retires the moment the counter drops, so the person sees why the line appeared and why it left. The `soon` line states the exact firing condition ('3 src edits unchecked -> no-check nudge at 10m/14c') - the most transparent anti-surprise device in any design. `fails N ▸prefix` (normalised 40-char prefix, denials counted separately per C037/C038) and `uncommit +a −d · N files · Ne · Mm` (C032 git-tick) are the two rework counters the others lack as always-on numbers. Fixed within-class ordering with corpus priors is predictable, which matters more than optimal ranking for someone who hates nagging. Per-rule <=1-in-5 wrong-rate targets are tied to the specific corrections that achieve them (doc-only suppression, denial exclusion, structural-only correction markers, commits as tie-breakers only, plan-exit struck). Toasts NOW-only, no cache-miss toast, R03 via $.ui.log; loop-health replaces the slot. JSON carries source:{shim,hooks,transcript} per number so every renderer can say why a tile is '—'. Correct PRD citation (US-009 reserves `c`, State.view). R18 churn and R09 commit-without-check honestly flagged as unverified/LATER or gated. Mockup verified at 56 cells; recent log shrinks first at low heights.
scores.weaknesses: Two tile-dense rows at <=16 chars plus a 7-row recent log make it less corner-of-eye readable than Lights; the recent log is scanning load even though it is facts. `fails` tile turns red at 2 consecutive errors without the shared-prefix gate the slot uses, so legitimate probe chains (test -f / grep exit 1) will paint it red often. No limits tile (5h % appears only in the subscriber form of the ctx tile) for a Max-plan owner; no prefix tip (deliberately dashboard-only) and no explore-delegate. Square-corner frame `┌─` mismatches the rounded theme (theme.rs border_set ROUNDED with ASCII fallback); idle footer reads '↵ push' vs '↵ why' in the busy view. `1-6` jumping to panel-owned overlays needs view-switch plumbing (VIEW-01: overlays require an owning panel) that is glossed over. R09 rests on the phase model's 32% figure, not a verified candidate.
scores.steal: `soon` line phrased as the firing condition and threshold; `fails N ▸prefix` and `uncommit +a −d · N files · Ne · Mm` as the rework light's 1-key detail; per-number source:{shim,hooks,transcript} in the coach JSON with '—' semantics; fixed, published within-class ordering for NOW nudges instead of token-calls ranking; `1-6` jump from a light to the matching dashboard panel; a recent log restricted to nudge lifecycle (fired/acted/expired/snoozed) reachable behind a key, not on the main view; R09 commit-without-check once the C055 hand-label gate passes; the enumerated per-rule wrong-rate targets with the correction that gets each there.

judge:1.rationale: Judged as someone who lives in 6-hour Max-plan sessions and wants to be left alone: the deciding axes are false-positive resistance and glanceability, with data feasibility checked against tasks/research-coach/verdicts-done.json and the source audit (src/app.rs BINDINGS and key arms, src/ui/layout.rs solve(force: Option<Mode>), src/ask.rs copy_to_clipboard, theme.rs ROUNDED border set, docs/socket.md). All four mockups render at 56 cells (checked with an east-asian-width script; Lights' footer is 55). Lights (44) wins because its substrate - four re-evaluated state predicates that say nothing, one slot, a visible 'next' and 'snoozed' row, NOW-only toasts, per-turn budgets counted in human turns, and a fired/acted/snoozed audit trail - is the only frame in which the coach structurally cannot nag, and every nudge maps to the verified corrections without drift (C001 5m tightening, C002 dedupe/pricing, C003 tiers, C005 p50 19, C017 synthetic filter, C030 doc-only + degrade, C043 no commit-only, C050 no bare Bash, C055 test/build split, C058 loop signature, C062 NOW exemptions, C064 verb truncation). Its real gaps are a context light that would sit red all day on a 1M window and the absence of an explore-delegate nudge; both are fixable by grafting. Rework Radar (40) is a close second with the most transparent contract (counter -> keystroke -> retire) and the best `soon` line, but is denser and paints the fails tile red at 2 errors without the prefix gate. Phase Coach (39) has the widest lever coverage and two ideas worth stealing (the 4-in-5 wrong-rate bar and the acted/retired history), but carries four advice regions on screen, a static per-phase 'next:' line, a cache-miss toast, an explore-delegate action whose 'lands at the next API call' claim contradicts the C030 verdict (26/28 queued prompts land at turn end), and a $.turn.abort button that breaks the pane's read-only stance. Ticker (35) has the best single decision number (`next 19c vs fresh`) and the tape, but its cost-first ranking demotes rework signals, its tiles carry no edits/fails counters, it toasts after-the-fact cache misses, its $ frame is notional for this subscriber, and `t`/`?` collide with global keys.

scores.strengths: Best corner-of-the-eye read at 56 cols: four label-aligned rows whose glyph (○◐●) encodes state monochrome with colour on top, one slot, deliberate whitespace, 'next' and 'snoozed' rows that make silence visibly the person's choice. Reuses the existing rounded frame, title-in-border, ◆ WAITING pill (header.rs:31) and 3 s footer toast (TOAST_MS) — all verified. Every mockup line measures 56 cells. Nudge model follows the corrections exactly: C001 5m-TTL tightening, C005 656/669 + p50 19, C030 doc-only suppression and 'queue' wording, C041 '—' without the shim and '(cold)' pricing, C060 spend-limit branch, C062/C064 single-writer advisor.json. Lights are states and cannot nag; family cooldown shared between L-CTX-01/02; 1 LATER per 2 turns; NOW exempt from first-2-turn/away suppression. Events-row audit trail + SessionEnd tally ('7 fired, 4 acted, 2 snoozed') is the only design with a built-in tuning loop. Risk list is honest and accurate (OSC 52 blocked in Apple Terminal, ambiguous-width glyphs, writer race).
scores.weaknesses: Uses `v` where tasks/prd-cctop-coach.md US-009 reserves `c` (both keys are free in BINDINGS, but it deviates from the PRD). No explore-delegate nudge although explore is 51% of positive context growth (session-phase-model) and name-based A05 fires 0% here; no plan-first, churn or commit-without-check. Keys row inside the slot ('Enter copy · x snooze · e why  NOW · +1') duplicates the footer and 'NOW · +1' is cryptic. Ranking by tokens × remaining calls systematically favours context/cache over rework within a class (admitted, unmeasured). Ignores the existing ask.rs socket send path ('S') that Ticker reuses. Rows 12–16 blank at 56x20 may read as empty to the owner (mitigated by the 'next' row).
scores.steal: The four-light strip itself (state glyph + colour, never rate-limited) as the always-on layer under any slot; the 'snoozed' row with remaining cooldown; 'next' row showing the promoted-on-retire candidate; Events/SessionEnd audit rows for every fire/acted/snooze; L0/L1/L2 status-line reductions that change only on level/slot change (no flicker); family-shared cooldowns (context-reset); 1-4 light focus for on-demand detail; toast on NOW promotion only.

scores.strengths: Broadest lever coverage: the only design with N-EXPLORE-DELEGATE (explore = 51% of context growth; Grep/Glob absent in all 113 transcripts so the Bash-aware class is mandatory), plus N-PLAN-FEATURE (dim, per C033 correction) and N-COMMIT-GREEN. Enter marks the nudge 'acting' and waits for its acted predicate; the idle view shows 'acted · cargo test ran 31 s later' / 'retired · Explore agent spawned' so a fooled coach is visible. Wrong-rate bar (≥4 in 5 in the corpus to take the ▸ slot, else dim line) is an explicit anti-nag policy. Data-prerequisite paragraph is the most complete and accurate (tools.rs 30-char clip, hooks.rs:75 strip, Mode::Coach via layout::solve force, config persist like 'w', existing 40x24/60x51/122x37 snapshots). Uses PRD key `c`. All 20 mockup rows measure 56 cells.
scores.weaknesses: Densest screen: 17 populated rows, three state lines, bar + two figures per tile, a 2-line NEXT and a 2-line soon — it must be read, not glanced. The passive per-phase 'next:' line contradicts the slot in the busy mockup ('let it run — a check lands ≤2 calls after edits' while 14 calls have passed and the ▸ says queue the test) and is always-on advice-shaped text that will become wallpaper. Two advice slots (NOW + NEXT line) dilute 'exactly one nudge'. The phase gate makes every nudge's eligibility depend on the classifier that is weakest where it matters (verify 47–56%); the 94% figure is self-consistency, as it admits. 24 nudges is the largest surface for wrong fires. 'bg tasks / crons' tiles are hook-only.
scores.steal: N-EXPLORE-DELEGATE (8+ explore-class calls, ≥20k run tokens, no Edit/Agent → 'use an Explore subagent for the rest'); acted-vs-retired history lines in the idle slot; Enter → 'acting' state cleared by the acted predicate; the ≥4-in-5 corpus wrong-rate bar as a hard gate for the ▸ slot; N-COMMIT-GREEN trigger (green test + ≥5 edits + ≥30 min); engine-native pane overrides ($.session.usage, turn.step, tool.check, Spinner.mode); per-nudge 'right 10/10 last month / fires ~15×/month' in the explain overlay.

scores.strengths: Only design that reuses the existing ask popup end-to-end: Enter pre-fills action text, Enter copies (ask::copy_to_clipboard), `S` sends over the messaging socket (ask.rs send_over_socket, app.rs:308) — a real act path the others discard. 'next 19c ≈$4.4 · fresh $0.9' is the cleanest continue-vs-/clear decision number. Why overlay states the priced saving and the assumption behind it ('saves ≈3× assumes sonnet at the same tool count'). Dashboard Advisor panel mirrors the Ticker's primary nudge so the two views never disagree. `t` toggle to rate-limit units (fable 10 / opus 5 / sonnet 3 / haiku 1) per C014/C024. 7-day baseline multiplier uses baseline.rs cost_per_turn (exists). Slot changes only at turn boundaries or NOW events (no flicker). Tape rows are explicitly not a nudge channel. All 20 rows measure 56 cells.
scores.weaknesses: $-first framing is wrong for this owner by the design's own risk 2: all 8 status files carry rate_limits, so the default would be limit units and the mockup is not what the owner sees. Three separately framed boxes spend 6 of 20 rows on borders; tiles carry two figures each and the tape adds five timestamped dollar rows — numbers to parse, not state to see. Mockup inconsistency: tile 'agents ≈$117 86%' vs nudge header 'agents ≈$897 (86%)' (C014 says the $117 figure is stale). ctx-price re-fires every +100k (3–5×/long session, admitted 'marginal as a nudge'); cache-miss toasts on every ≥20k miss; ×3.2 multiplier is hidden until ≥3 sessions. Thinnest rework coverage: no steers, commit, churn, explore or plan-first nudges. Ranking by 'largest priced saving' is systematically notional on a subscription.
scores.steal: Enter → existing ask popup with copy + `S` socket send (copy-only for slash/settings); 'next N calls ≈$X · fresh $Y' pair on the context tile; `t` $/limit-unit toggle defaulting to limit units when rate_limits is present; Advisor panel showing the coach's primary nudge as its first row; why overlay listing the priced saving plus its stated assumption; tape/Events rows opening the same why overlay; '(cold: next call ≈$2.0)' tile variant.

scores.strengths: Strongest rework coverage: adds R09 commit-without-check (32% of commit calls had no check in the previous 10 calls per the phase model ACT line) and R18 churn, keeps rewind info paired with corrections, splits fails vs denied in one tile. Counters-with-corpus-lines means every nudge retires the moment its tile drops — the most self-evidently honest retirement model. Explicit ≤1-in-5 wrong-rate target per rule with the exact corrections that get it there (doc-only 69%, denial exclusion, structural-only corrections, commits as tie-breakers, plan exit removed from cold list). Fixed within-class order is predictable. No-check is NEXT (amber mid-turn, slot at turn end) — more conservative than Lights' NOW. Uses the PRD-reserved `c` and State.view per VIEW-01/US-009; JSON carries source:{shim,hooks,transcript} so each renderer can say why a tile is '—'. R09/R18 honestly flagged as unverified and kept low.
scores.weaknesses: Claims to put key hints in the bottom border 'exactly as the dashboard footer does' — the dashboard footer is a separate dim line (app.rs draw_footer), and it draws square corners where theme.border_set() defaults to ROUNDED. Idle bottom border measures 57 cells and its footer says '↵ push' vs the busy view's '↵ why'. Enter = why (not act) diverges from the other three designs and from its own PRD line 295 ('a copies or sends'). The 7-row recent log is dim but still fills a third of the screen with fail/steer/churn facts on a busy turn. No explore-delegate nudge; prefix left to the dashboard. R18 churn residual is thin once .md is skipped (RW-06: 4 of the 6 ≥8-edit files are .md).
scores.steal: R09 commit-without-check as a NOW nudge; the ≤1-in-5 per-rule wrong-rate target written next to each rule with its corrections; source:{shim,hooks,transcript} per number so '—' is explained; fixed within-class priority list instead of a token-weighted formula for rework nudges; 'retired: 2 acted · 1 expired · 0 snoozed' tally in the idle slot; 'fails N ▸prefix / denied N' tile split; 3rd snooze = rest of session; `l` toggle between fact log and nudge lifecycle.

judge:3.rationale: Judged as a TUI at 56 columns read from the corner of the eye, Lights wins on the two things a coach view must get right first — glanceability and not nagging — while staying feasible against the verified candidates. Its four state lights are pure predicates that cannot nag, its single slot plus visible 'next'/'snoozed' rows make silence legible, and every trigger/wording matches the verdict corrections (C001, C005, C030, C041, C060, C062, C064); all busy-mockup rows measure exactly 56 cells and the frame/pill/toast conventions it cites exist in src (header.rs:31, TOAST_MS, ROUNDED border set). Radar is a close second with the strongest rework coverage and the most self-evidently honest retirement (counter drops → nudge gone) but has cosmetic convention errors (keys-in-border, square corners, 57-cell idle border, inconsistent Enter). Phase Coach has the broadest lever coverage — it is the only design that addresses explore-in-main-context, 51% of context growth — but is too dense to glance and its always-on per-phase 'next:' line contradicts its own slot in the mockup. Ticker's $-first framing is notional for this subscriber by its own admission, spends six rows on borders, and covers rework thinly; its socket-send act path and 'fresh $0.9' comparison are the ideas worth grafting. Grafts for the winner: Phase Coach's explore-delegate nudge and acted/retired history, Radar's commit-without-check and per-rule ≤1-in-5 bar with source-per-tile, Ticker's ask-popup act path with `S` send and the limit-unit default, and switch Lights' toggle key from `v` to the PRD-reserved `c`.

scores.strengths: Cleanest separation of state from advice: four lights are pure predicates re-evaluated every tick and never rate-limited, so they cannot nag, while exactly one nudge slot (headline / exact action / keys, 'NOW · +1') and one 'next' row carry all advice. Glyph-encoded state (○◐●) is monochrome-safe and readable from the corner of the eye; 5 deliberately empty rows. Every nudge cites the light it belongs to so the evidence is on screen. Corrections from every cited verdict are applied faithfully (C001 5m-TTL tightening and no countdown >300 s; C002 dedupe by message.id and write-rate pricing; C003 two tiers, plan-exit removed; C005 p50 19 not 32, subscriber phrasing; C030 doc-only suppression and degrade-to-strip when no test cmd; C032 git tick not gitOperation; C035 structural-only markers; C037 denial exclusion; C043 commits as tie-breaker; C050 no bare Bash; C057 human-turn identity; C058 loop signature; C060 spend-limit branch; C062 NOW exemptions, shown-per-turn). Verified: 'v' is unbound in src/app.rs (only ?,1-9,Tab,Esc,p,w,+,-,q,a,t,L,Ctrl-C and panel-local j/k/n/N/x/s/S/i/g/G/d/f); ask.rs copy_to_clipboard exists for the Enter fallback; VIEW-01 explicitly recommends the State.view pattern it uses; mockups measure 20 rows × 56 cells. 'Snoozed' row makes silence visibly the person's choice; Events audit trail (fired/acted/snoozed) enables later tuning. Rework light goes red only on structural events until the ~200-call hand-label gate — honest about C041/C055's 47 % verify agreement.
scores.weaknesses: Always-on strip omits the two dollar figures an API payer wants: subagent spend (C014: 13.7 % of corpus, 86 % of this session; only a LATER nudge and a 'failed spawns' token here) and $/turn or session $ (no baseline multiplier). No passive 'what to do when quiet' guidance — idle just says 'nothing to do'. The rework light cell is overwritten by streak text ('3 fails') so the edits/✓ figure disappears exactly when both matter. Ranking within a class by tokens × remaining calls systematically favours context/cache over rework nudges (acknowledged, unmeasured). No explore-delegate or plan-first lever. Uses fixed 150k/300k bands although C041's correction says to mirror the binary's threshold − 20k (they layer both, acceptable). Toggle key 'v' diverges from the coach PRD's US-009 which reserves 'c' (tasks/prd-cctop-coach.md:398). Ambiguous-width glyphs (○◐●◆▸↻✓) need the ASCII fallback they promise. Footer rows measure 55 cells (trivial).
scores.steal: n/a (winner). Keep intact: lights-as-predicates, single slot + next + snoozed rows, per-light detail on 1-4, Events audit trail, degrade-to-'—' rule. Graft the items listed under the other three designs.

scores.strengths: Broadest lever coverage of the four: adds N-EXPLORE-DELEGATE (phase model verified: 46 main-context explore runs ≥ 8 calls at p50 48.7k tokens vs Explore agent returning p50 71 tokens) and N-PLAN-FEATURE (C033 verified, 11 fires/month, correctly rendered as a dim P2 line), plus commit-green, review, drift, loop-health, and turn/session $ tiles. Strongest FP framework on paper: a per-nudge phase gate (N-CHECK never in VERIFY, N-CHECKPOINT only after a clean end_turn), a wrong-rate bar (≥ 4 in 5 in the corpus to take the ▸ slot, else dim NEXT line), and an idle state that shows acted vs retired with the observable completion ('acted · cargo test ran 31 s later') so a fooled coach is visible. Passive per-phase 'next:' default line always tells the person what to expect without spending the nudge budget. Enter marks the nudge 'acting' and waits for its acted predicate — real feedback. Data prerequisites listed as one honest block (C055 200-char command, C056/C057 ingestion, C017 synthetic filter, UNS-13, GAP-01, C032 tick, C062/C064 fields); Mode::Coach via layout::solve's force: Option<Mode> matches the C064 correction; 'c' verified free (src/app.rs binds only Ctrl-C). Mockups measure exactly 20 × 56 with the tile widths C041's correction demands (≤ 26 chars).
scores.weaknesses: Busiest surface: all 20 rows used, a 3-line ▸ slot with a file list, NEXT and soon sections, section-title dividers — readable while typing only via the phase word and the amber tile. Internal contradiction: N-EXPLORE-DELEGATE tells the person a mid-turn line 'lands at Claude's next API call' while N-CHECK (same design) cites C030's finding that queued prompts land at turn end 26/28 times — so the mid-turn NOW explore nudge mostly arrives after the run's cost is sunk; the phase model also flags the 'Explore agent returns p50 71 tok' figure as an open question (possibly truncated toolUseResult). The wrong-rate bar is asserted, not evidenced, for most nudges (only N-SWITCH-WARM 10/10 and N-REVIEW 60/81 have corpus precision). Phase gating rests on a 94 % self-consistency classifier (C041: not hand labels), so a wrong phase can silence a valid nudge. Largest implementation surface (phase detector + 24 nudges + three sections + acted history) — the most likely to ship late or half-wired.
scores.steal: (1) Passive per-phase 'next:' default line (EXPLORE 'let it run · at 8 reads say: use an Explore subagent', IDLE 'same task? keep typing · new? /rename → /clear') as the Lights slot's dim filler when no nudge is due. (2) Wrong-rate bar: a nudge needs ≥ 4-in-5 corpus precision to take the slot, else it renders as the 'next' row only. (3) Per-nudge phase gate (never N-CHECK while a test-class Bash is the last call). (4) Idle 'acted · <completion>' / 'retired · <reason>' history lines in Lights' empty rows. (5) Enter → 'acting' state that waits for the acted predicate and reports it. (6) N-EXPLORE-DELEGATE re-timed as a turn-end/NEXT nudge (queue lands at turn end) and N-PLAN-FEATURE as a dim next-row item. (7) ▇▇▁▁ context bar and the `$` turn/session toggle. (8) The snapshot fixture list (8-call explore run, Edit→cargo test→commit, unverified commit, AskUserQuestion with > 1 h gap, /clear, TaskUpdate completed, <synthetic> zero-usage line).

scores.strengths: The only design that prices the biggest wallet items on the always-on strip: an agents tile (C014: agents ≈ 86 % of this session's spend, failed spawns excluded), 'next 19c ≈$4.4 · fresh $0.9' (continue-vs-fresh is the single decision number for the 51.6 %-of-spend lever, C005), and 'turn ≈$2.61 ×3.2 7d' — feasible today, and easier than its own risk #4 admits: src/baseline.rs already computes cost_per_turn/tokens_per_turn medians with MIN_TURNS=3 and a multiplier() helper. `t` toggle between $ and rate-limit units handles the subscriber/API split cleanly. The tape of priced events (≥ 20k tok / ≥ $0.10, newest first, Enter opens the why) is an audit trail a lead can use to explain a bill without being told what to do. Anti-flicker rule (slot changes only at a human-turn boundary or a NOW event) and the '≤ 3 distinct nudges per 10 human turns' budget are good additions. Enter reusing the existing ask popup is real (src/ask.rs: compose, copy_to_clipboard, send_over_socket; docs/socket.md exists). 'c' verified free; mockups measure 20 × 56.
scores.weaknesses: Least glanceable: three bordered frames spend 6 of 20 rows on chrome, six tiles each carry a core plus suffix, and the nudge slot's third line leaks a research ID into the UI ('saves ≈3× per agent call · C014'). Mockup inconsistency: 'agents ≈$117 86%' mixes the stale $117 figure C014's verdict retired with the live 86 % share (the corrected pair is ≈$897 / 86 %). Ranking within a class by priced saving structurally pushes rework nudges (no $ figure) to the bottom, and correction-streak is classed NEXT where ctx-price will out-rank it — so the rework lever rarely reaches the slot. Rework coverage is thinner: no steers (C059), no commit-tail nudge, no silent-run liveness on the state line, no loop-health indicator, no explore-delegate. ctx-price re-fires at every +100k (3–5 times in a deliberate long session — acknowledged as 'marginal as a nudge'). The 'S' send-over-socket path, while pre-existing, is the one channel that writes into the session and sits uneasily with the read-only stance the other designs keep. Tape can fill in screenshot- or loop-heavy sessions.
scores.steal: (1) Agents tile as a fifth Lights light or state-line token: 'agents ≈$897 86% · 3 run · 174 failed' from the recursive subagents/** scan with <synthetic> spawns excluded (C014). (2) 'next 19c ≈$4.4 · fresh $0.9' as the context light's focus detail (session p50 calls per long run × $/call vs the same run at post-/clear ctx p50 45k). (3) '×N 7d' baseline multiplier on the turn figure using baseline.rs cost_per_turn + multiplier(). (4) `t` toggle $ ↔ rate-limit units, defaulting to units when rate_limits is present. (5) '(cold: next call ≈$2.0)' form of the per-call tile when prompt_cache.warm is false. (6) Priced-event tape as Events rows of kind=cost (cache miss with cause + $, cold write, agent batch, top-5 % turn, model switch, loop fires) and Enter-on-row why. (7) Anti-flicker rule (slot changes only at human-turn boundary or NOW) and the ≤ 3-per-10-turns budget. (8) Toast for a priced cache miss the moment turn.step reports it.

scores.strengths: Cleanest retirement semantic of the four: every nudge names the keystroke or typed line that resets a visible counter, so predicate-false retirement is intrinsic and the person can see why a nudge vanished. The six counters expose the rework precursors the other designs hide: 'fails 2 ▸gh pr view' with the failing prefix and denials counted apart (C037/C038/C050 corrections), 'uncommit +a −d · N files · Ne · Mm' blast radius from the 5-s git tick (C032 corrections), 'edits N ✓age'. Fixed intra-class priority order (R05 > R04 > R01 > …) is predictable and keeps rework nudges from being out-ranked by priced ones. Most explicit about not double-firing with A01–A18 (R01 subsumes A15, R11 replaces A02's timing, R22 replaces A01, R10 replaces A18, R19 replaces A14, R12's pre half → A06 wording). Adds R09 commit-without-check (phase model verified: 175 of 548 commit calls, 32 %, had no verify in the preceding 10 calls; ~1 commit per 12 turns after C032's correction) and keeps R18 churn honestly at LATER as an unverified addition. Toggle 'c' matches the coach PRD (US-009 at tasks/prd-cctop-coach.md:398) and is verified free; JSON carries a source field ({shim, hooks, transcript}) so each renderer can say why a tile is blank. Wrong-rate ≤ 1-in-5 per rule is tied to specific corrections (doc-only suppression, denial exclusion, structural-only markers, commit as tie-breaker, plan exit removed from R17). 'Recent' fact log shrinks first at low heights. Mockups measure 20 × 56.
scores.weaknesses: Least aligned with an API payer's wallet: rework dollars are small (C030: a correction turn is median $0.49, p90 $3.47) while the strip shows no $/turn, no session $, no baseline multiplier and no agents spend (R19 is LATER only) — the 51.6 %-above-300k and 86 %-agents levers appear only as 'ctx 412k $.21/c' and a retrospective nudge. No explore-delegate; prefix tip deliberately pushed to the dashboard. R18 churn is built on mining counts, not a verified candidate, and the ≥ 8-edit files are mostly docs (md 4, yaml 1, rs 1 of 6) — with .md/.txt excluded it will rarely fire (fine, but it is design weight for little return). R16 cache-countdown is classed NEXT though C001 frames it as act-within-minutes, so a NOW fail cascade would hide a 4-minute cache cliff. Footer inconsistency between mockups ('↵ why' vs '↵ push'). Denser than Lights: the recent log makes it a reading surface, not a corner-of-eye one, and 1–6 drill into dashboard overlays adds modal depth.
scores.steal: (1) 'fails N ▸prefix / denied M' as the rework light's detail (normalised 40-char command prefix of the last error; denials counted apart). (2) 'uncommit +412 −87 · 9 files · 18 edits · 42m' / 'clean · committed 3m ago' from the git tick as the commit-tail evidence cell. (3) R09 commit-without-check (gitOperation.commit with edits_since_verify > 0 and no test-class call in the last 10). (4) Fixed intra-class priority order instead of tokens × remaining-calls ranking, so rework nudges keep their place. (5) The explicit A01–A18 overlap-resolution table (subsume/replace/reword) as a shipping checklist. (6) Dim 'recent' fact rows (steer / fail / denied / commit / verify / acted / expired / snoozed) in Lights' empty rows, first to shrink at < 20 rows. (7) '▸ steer window' marker on calls 1–5 of a run (PH-14) and the 'render.rs ×5' churn token in the state line. (8) `source` field per number in the coach JSON so a blank tile explains itself. (9) R08 gating: degrade to strip text when neither a session test command nor a CLAUDE.md test line exists.

judge:2.rationale: Persona: a team lead paying API list prices for eight people. Two things decide this: (a) the view must survive contact with eight people who did not design it — if it nags or reads like a table it gets closed, and a closed coach saves nothing; (b) the dollars sit in context volume (C005: calls > 300k are 25.5 % of calls and 51.6 % of spend), cold cache (14.6 % of spend) and subagents (13.7 % corpus, 86 % of this session), while rework dollars are small per event (median $0.49 per correction turn). Lights wins on the rubric (41 vs 40/40/34) because it is the only design built to be read from the corner of the eye — four glyph-encoded predicates that cannot nag, one slot, one 'next' row, and visible snoozes — while applying every verdict correction as faithfully as the others and keeping the two biggest always-on levers (ctx with ≈$/call, cache warmth) in view. Its gaps are graftable without changing its shape: Ticker's agents tile and continue-vs-fresh price ('next 19c ≈$4.4 · fresh $0.9', plus the ×N 7d multiplier that src/baseline.rs already supports via cost_per_turn and multiplier()), Phase Coach's passive per-phase 'next:' line, wrong-rate bar and acted/retired history in the empty rows, and Radar's fixed intra-class priority order, fails/uncommit counters, commit-without-check nudge and A01–A18 overlap table. Phase Coach is the most complete and has the best FP machinery on paper (phase gate, ≥ 4-in-5 bar, acted history) but is the busiest surface, the largest build, and carries one internal contradiction (its mid-turn explore-delegate nudge assumes queued text lands at the next API call while its own N-CHECK cites C030's 26/28 turn-end finding; the phase model also flags the 'Explore agent returns 71 tok' figure as an open question). Rework Radar has the cleanest retirement semantic (nudge names the keystroke that resets a visible counter) and the strongest overlap hygiene, but its always-on strip shows none of the dollar levers beyond $/call and its added churn nudge is unverified and mostly a docs-file phenomenon. Ticker is the design an API payer most wants to read for the bill (agents, next-run price, baseline multiplier, tape) but the worst to keep open: three bordered frames, priced-saving ranking that buries rework nudges, a research ID leaked into the UI, and a stale '$117 / 86 %' pair in its own mockup. Verification performed: all eight mockups measured at 20 rows × 56 cells (footers ±1); 'c' bound only as Ctrl-C and 'v' unbound in src/app.rs; coach PRD US-009 reserves 'c' (tasks/prd-cctop-coach.md:398); ask.rs has compose/copy_to_clipboard/send_over_socket and docs/socket.md exists; baseline.rs has cost_per_turn/tokens_per_turn medians and multiplier(); phase-model figures (46 explore runs ≥ 8 calls, p50 48.7k; Explore agent p50 71 tok; 32 % of commit calls unchecked; interrupts p50 3 calls) and rework-mining churn counts (15 files ≥ 8 edits, 37 turn/file ≥ 4, 67 E→R→E, 126 redundant reads; ≥ 8-edit files md 4 / yaml 1 / rs 1) confirmed in the reader reports; every 'see verdicts-done.json' candidate (C001, C002, C003, C005, C007, C010, C014, C016, C017, C018, C023, C030, C032) read and its corrections compared against each design's trigger text — all four apply them; differences are in framing, ranking and surface, not in data claims.
